id: Mishneh Torah, Those Who Defile Bed or Seat 11:5
q_practical: If someone I don't know well tells me a jar is clean, can I trust them?
q_conceptual: Why would an ordinary person's word be trusted about cleanliness in one city but not elsewhere?

q_practical: If I injure my employee twice in one incident, do I owe compensation for both injuries?
q_conceptual: Why would causing two separate injuries trigger two completely different kinds of remedy?

q_practical: Does a letter count as delivered once it lands in my yard, even if I never touched it?
q_conceptual: Why would crossing a property boundary, rather than being received by hand, decide when a document takes effect?

q_practical: Can I insist on buying the house next door instead of the stranger who already agreed to buy it?
q_conceptual: Why would living next to a property give someone a legal right to override a completed sale?

q_practical: Am I allowed to stop my animal from eating while it works, even if the food isn't fully mine to give away?
q_conceptual: Why would an animal's right to eat while it works not depend on who legally owns the food?

q_practical: Can someone be married off without ever being told about it?
q_conceptual: Why would consent matter even in a relationship where one party has very little power to refuse?

q_practical: If money set aside for one purpose accidentally gets spent on something else, does the mix-up still count as valid?
q_conceptual: Why would a mistake be treated as more forgivable than the same act done on purpose?

id: Mishneh Torah, Vessels of the Sanctuary and Those Who Serve Therein 4:14
q_practical: What's the one practical difference between the two ways someone could take on this senior religious office?
q_conceptual: Why would the method used to install someone in a role change what's required of them later, when everything else about the role stays the same?

q_practical: If I miss a deadline in an agreement because of illness or a flood, does the agreement still take effect as written?
q_conceptual: Why wouldn't a good excuse change the outcome once a conditional agreement's deadline has passed?

id: Mishneh Torah, Sabbatical Year and the Jubilee 12:6
q_practical: If I sell two properties a few weeks apart during a leap year, do their contracts run out on the same date?
q_conceptual: Why would an extra month added to the calendar change how a deadline gets counted?

q_practical: Should I observe mourning when my spouse's parent dies, even though it isn't my own parent?
q_conceptual: Why would grief be expressed out of respect for someone else's loss, rather than only for blood relatives?

id: Mishneh Torah, Sabbatical Year and the Jubilee 1:8
q_practical: Can I water my orchard during a year when I'm supposed to leave the land alone?
q_conceptual: Why would how closely trees are planted together determine how much watering is allowed?

id: Mishneh Torah, Murderer and the Preservation of Life 12:9
q_practical: Can I get treatment from a doctor outside my faith community if my life is at risk?
q_conceptual: Why would the rules differ between an outsider and someone who has actively rejected shared beliefs?

id: Mishneh Torah, Robbery and Lost Property 15:10
q_practical: I found a bundle of stuff on someone else's property - can I keep it, or do I have to report finding it?
q_conceptual: Why would the way an object appears to have gotten somewhere change whether you're allowed to keep it?

q_practical: Something spilled into my pool and changed its color - is it still usable for its intended purpose?
q_conceptual: Why would the color of water matter for whether it can still serve a ritual function?

q_practical: If barely any blood came out when I slaughtered an animal, do I still have to cover it up afterward?
q_conceptual: Why would even a small amount of blood trigger the same obligation as a large amount?

id: Mishneh Torah, Those Who Defile Bed or Seat 11:11

q_conceptual: Why would public contact with something require a cleansing ritual afterward, with one exception made for a single prized item?

q_practical: If rain falls on crops I left outside without me wanting it to, does that change their status?
q_conceptual: Why would intention matter more than the physical event itself, and why would some people's intentions simply not count?

id: Mishneh Torah, Woman Suspected of Infidelity 3:5

q_conceptual: Why would this be turned into a public spectacle rather than handled privately?

q_conceptual: Why would the material of just the corners, rather than the garment as a whole, decide the obligation?

q_practical: What extra prayers get added on a day when the whole community is fasting?
q_conceptual: Why leave room for someone's own choice of words rather than requiring only fixed text?

q_practical: I paid someone with a coin that turned out to be underweight - can they still hand it back to me months later?
q_conceptual: Why would being able to identify the exact coin change whether it can be returned?

q_practical: How should I treat someone who just lost a parent or spouse, even if they're financially secure?
q_conceptual: Why single out this group for extra sensitivity, and why doesn't their wealth exempt them from that care?

id: Mishneh Torah, Appraisals and Devoted Property 7:13
q_practical: If something's value changes between when I agree to buy it and when I actually take it, which price applies?
q_conceptual: Why would the moment of payment, rather than the moment of taking possession, lock in the price?

id: Mishneh Torah, Ownerless Property and Gifts 6:11
q_practical: If my inheritance was split among my siblings and one of them dies before our parent does, can I claim from that sibling's share?
q_conceptual: Why wouldn't an earlier gift fully cancel out a later claim on part of the estate?

q_practical: If something gets mixed into my wine that changes how it's made, can I now share a drink with someone outside my group?
q_conceptual: Why would a small additive be enough to change what's considered acceptable?

q_practical: If I'm not sure whether my vineyard broke a planting rule, do I have to assume the worst?
q_conceptual: Why would the same uncertainty be resolved differently depending on where you live?

q_practical: Can I 'give' someone money that's sitting somewhere else without physically handing it to them?
q_conceptual: Why would owning land let you indirectly acquire money stored on it, while assigning someone a debt not work the same way?

id: Mishneh Torah, Daily Offerings and Additional Offerings 10:8

q_conceptual: Why would deviating from one small physical detail be read as expressing a whole theological disagreement?

q_practical: Can I still use water that passed through a natural filter, or does that count as being processed?
q_conceptual: Why would something that changes water's color or path still not count as putting it in a container?

q_practical: If I sew a bunch of small fabric scraps together into a blanket, does it count as one piece of fabric?
q_conceptual: Why would sewing scraps together be treated the same as weaving a single piece?

q_practical: Can a legal form be filled out in advance with blanks for names, or does it have to be written fresh each time?
q_conceptual: Why wouldn't leaving blanks for names undermine an otherwise personal legal document?

q_practical: Can neighbors combine their private spaces so they can carry things between each other's homes, and how is that set up?
q_conceptual: Why would where an object is stored determine whether this kind of arrangement actually works?

q_practical: What could someone say to show they approve of a commitment their spouse made?
q_conceptual: Why would specific spoken words matter for confirming agreement, rather than just staying silent?

q_practical: Can daughters receive the same portion as sons from this?
q_conceptual: Why would this particular benefit be extended equally to daughters when other privileges are more restricted?

id: Mishneh Torah, Sabbatical Year and the Jubilee 8:17

q_conceptual: Why would we assume dishonesty about self-interest but not assume it for disinterested testimony?

id: Mishneh Torah, Murderer and the Preservation of Life 9:12
q_practical: Why would a ceremony be cancelled once a certain kind of crime became too common?
q_conceptual: Why would even an otherwise unreliable witness be enough to call off a ritual meant for unsolved cases?

id: Mishneh Torah, Robbery and Lost Property 15:7
q_practical: I found a knife buried in a pile of trash - can I keep it, or do I have to report it?
q_conceptual: Why would whether the trash is normally cleared out affect whether something in it counts as abandoned?

q_practical: If two people lie under oath one right after the other, are they both equally responsible?
q_conceptual: Why would the timing between two people's statements change their legal responsibility?

q_practical: My dog bites different people on different days - at what point does it count as a known biter?
q_conceptual: Why would a pattern spread across alternating days, rather than happening every time, still count as establishing a habit?

q_practical: Can I eat the crispy coating on a piece of roasted meat, or just the meat itself?
q_conceptual: Why would the type of coating used change whether it absorbed something forbidden?

q_practical: If someone becomes eligible to participate right on the day of a ceremony, can they still join at the last moment?
q_conceptual: Why would becoming ready just in time still not be soon enough?

q_practical: Can I pray in a room where there's a dirty diaper?
q_conceptual: Why would a small child's waste be treated more leniently than an adult's?

q_practical: I'm technically allowed to do something, but should I still avoid it because of how it looks to others?
q_conceptual: Why would something permitted in principle still require extra care because of appearances?

id: Mishneh Torah, Daily Offerings and Additional Offerings 3:17
q_practical: What was the exact procedure for relighting a lamp if it went out?
q_conceptual: Why would relighting be split into two separate stages rather than done all at once?

q_practical: What were the different ways someone could legally take on or release this kind of servant?
q_conceptual: Why would a minor in this status be treated more like property than an adult would be?

id: Mishneh Torah, Sabbatical Year and the Jubilee 12:3
q_practical: If the person I made a deal with dies, can I still complete the arrangement with their child?
q_conceptual: Why would a right like this pass to an heir rather than simply expiring?

q_conceptual: Why would the exact moment something goes wrong determine who ends up affected by it?

q_practical: Is being allowed to eat something and being allowed to prepare it always the same permission?
q_conceptual: Why would there be exceptions running in both directions of an otherwise matching rule?

q_practical: If I find a bird sitting on eggs in an unusual arrangement, am I allowed to take them?
q_conceptual: Why would the arrangement of the eggs, not just the fact of finding them, determine whether taking them is allowed?

id: Mishneh Torah, Ownerless Property and Gifts 9:16
q_practical: Once I've formally finalized giving something away on my deathbed, can I still change my mind?
q_conceptual: Why would a formal completion step remove the flexibility that a deathbed gift usually allows?

id: Mishneh Torah, Appraisals and Devoted Property 5:14
q_practical: If I only dedicate part of something, does the whole thing become off-limits?
q_conceptual: Why would an unresolved legal question be settled by defaulting to the stricter outcome?

q_practical: Do I have to set aside a portion of my vegetable garden the same way I would for a grain field?
q_conceptual: Why would the specific wording of a rule limit it to certain crops and exclude others?

q_practical: How much of an internal tendon has to be cut before an animal is no longer fit to eat?
q_conceptual: Why would cutting most of something, rather than all of it, be the deciding line?

q_practical: Does a donation from someone outside the community count the same as one from within it?
q_conceptual: Why would the same act of dedicating something carry different legal weight depending on what it was meant for?

q_practical: How far apart do my rows of grapevines need to be before they count as two separate plots instead of one?
q_conceptual: Why would spacing alone determine whether two things are treated as a single unit or as distinct?

id: Mishneh Torah, Tefillin, Mezuzah and the Torah Scroll 10:2
q_practical: Can I sell a family heirloom to cover an important expense, or only as an absolute last resort?
q_conceptual: Why would only certain specific purposes justify selling something otherwise considered untouchable?

q_practical: Does my jacket need these tassels, or is it too small or the wrong material to require them?
q_conceptual: Why would a rule apply only above a certain size and only to certain fabrics?

q_practical: Does it matter what color the inside of a strap is if no one normally sees it?
q_conceptual: Why would appearance matter even for a part of something that's meant to stay hidden?

q_practical: Is an extra offering always brought alongside the main one, or only under certain conditions?
q_conceptual: Why would circumstances like the day of the week or the supply on hand change what's required?

q_practical: Is silently hating someone actually wrong, even if I never say or do anything about it?
q_conceptual: Why would something be called a violation but carry no punishment for it?

q_practical: Can I still cut through my neighbor's path in the evening once the dew has started to fall?
q_conceptual: Why would a natural sign like dew mark the exact moment a permission ends?

q_practical: If a fire I started spreads and destroys something nearby, am I responsible even though it wasn't right next to what I was burning?
q_conceptual: Why would liability depend on whether something was located where it's normally expected to be?

id: Mishneh Torah, The Sanhedrin and the Penalties within Their Jurisdiction 22:3
q_practical: If I notice my boss make a mistake, should I point it out right away or wait so I can take credit for fixing it?
q_conceptual: Why would delaying a correction, even to eventually fix it, count as a form of dishonesty?

q_practical: Does it matter where I carry out a task if doing it there might look like I'm copying another group's practice?
q_conceptual: Why would the same act become suspect purely because of where it's performed?

q_practical: If I said something false to avoid a fee, but later correct myself, will the correction be believed?
q_conceptual: Why would the assumed motive behind an earlier false statement affect whether a later correction is trusted?

id: Mishneh Torah, Vessels of the Sanctuary and Those Who Serve Therein 8:18
q_practical: What exactly did this piece of priestly clothing cover?
q_conceptual: Why would something so basic in design still need such precise specification?

id: Mishneh Torah, Gifts to the Poor 9:11
